prompt: Improve an existing browser-based operations console used to start, monitor, cancel, and retry long-running jobs. Preserve direct URLs and browser history. The UI must represent queued, running, partial, stale, completed, failed, cancellation-requested, cancellation-failed, and retrying states; survive refresh; recover focus after dialogs or navigation; handle slow and failed network requests; and work at narrow and wide supported viewports. Use the repository's existing framework and design system. Produce an implementation and real-browser verification contract without inventing backend behavior.

requirements: existing routes, framework, components, and tokens

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Direct URLs, browser history/back-forward behavior, refresh, and deep links preserve or recover the correct job/interface state using the existing routing model.

Queued, running, partial, stale, completed, failed, cancellation-requested, cancellation-failed, and retrying states are distinguishable and do not invent server-side cancellation/retry guarantees absent from the supplied backend contract.
Dialogs, navigation, cancellation/retry actions, loading/error feedback, and return flows use semantic controls with deterministic keyboard/focus restoration rather than click-only behavior.

Representative narrow/wide viewports, long/overflow content, slow requests, failed requests, refresh, and stale data preserve critical action/state access without layout-specific happy-path assumptions.

Verification exercises the real browser application with runtime/console evidence and the repository's existing framework/design system; static screenshots alone do not prove navigation, focus, async, or recovery behavior.

evidence: URL, history, refresh, and deep-link behavior
all required async and cancellation states
